solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Racing driver's plan put off a big bank

parts.note: Graham or Damon Hill, Formula One world champions, in the possessive

indicators.note: the letter given by the clue's 'a' is put off, i.e. removed from, the driver's plan

parts.note: a plan is an idea

explanation.surface: A racing driver's scheme for a big bank loan gets postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like 'postponed' but means 'removed': HILL'S IDEA loses its A. 'Big bank' is a slope of land, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank in the sense of a raised slope of ground; a big one is the sloping flank of a hill.

clue.text: Munching this with gin spoils good night

definitions.text: Munching this with gin spoils good night

indicators.note: spoils signals that the letters of good night are wrecked and rearranged, leaving room for the gin's letters to be found among them

explanation.surface: Eating junk food with a gin late at night ruins the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus GIN rearranges to GOOD NIGHT, and the whole clue describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter in a bun is late-night street food, and eating one with gin could well spoil the evening.

clue.text: Measure litres then stupidly put in gallons

indicators.note: put in tells us the gallons letter goes inside the jumbled word
stupidly says the word then is muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone converting volumes clumsily mixes litres with gallons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' makes ENTH from THEN, and 'put in' places G inside it: EN-G-TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is a dimension or extent that can be measured, so measure as a noun names it.

clue.text: Old gun in coach sawn off for deputy

indicators.note: in places the old gun inside the shortened carriage
sawn off says the carriage loses its end letter

parts.note: a surrey is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
gat is slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: An antique sawn-off shotgun is found in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sawn off' looks like it describes the shotgun, but it trims the carriage to SURRE; a surrey is an American horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute who acts in another's place, as a deputy does.

clue.text: Rebuff everyone with fine opening novel

indicators.note: opening says the fine letter comes at the start of everyone

parts.note: to rebuff an offer is to decline it
with means and
F is the abbreviation for fine (on pencil leads)
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Turning down everyone and opening with a fine sounds like a stern publisher's policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Evelyn Waugh's first, a 1928 satire; Gibbon's history shares the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's debut is a comic novel of that title, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Drive off and break speed limit, short of time

indicators.note: break shatters the words speed limit into pieces to be reassembled, once the letters of time are taken out of them

explanation.surface: A motorist drives away and breaks the speed limit, being in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: SPEED LIMIT, 'short of' TIME, leaves letters that rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or scatter, as sunshine banishes mist.

clue.text: Creamy yellow plant that climbs banks

indicators.note: banks means borders on both sides, so the climbing plant encloses the yellow

parts.note: ivy is a climbing evergreen plant
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A creamy yellow climbing plant grows up a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creamy yellow' looks like one colour; split it: 'Creamy' is the definition and 'yellow' gives OR, the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a creamy off-white colour, like elephant tusk, so a cream shade can be called this.

clue.text: Quaker statesman tours square before top brass

indicators.note: tours means goes around, so the statesman's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: William Penn, Quaker founder of Pennsylvania
a T-square, so T
ago means before, in the past

explanation.surface: A Quaker politician walks round a town square before meeting the generals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' gives T, after the T-square of the draughtsman; 'top brass' is the senior military, not a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the US Defense Department headquarters, so by metonymy it stands for the senior military command.

clue.text: Big ship at heart of ocean — the Bounty?

parts.note: big means large
SS is steamship

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, here of ocean

explanation.surface: A big ship in mid-ocean: surely HMS Bounty of mutiny fame?
explanation.walkthrough: The Bounty misleads as the famous mutiny ship; here it means generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounty is generous giving, and largesse is liberal giving of gifts or money: a synonym.

clue.text: Like Olivier in role of a prince in various "Harry" plays?

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in 'playing as Hamlet'

indicators.note: in puts the a-plus-prince pair inside the jumbled letters
various signals that the words Harry plays are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Laurence Olivier playing Prince Hal in several Shakespeare history plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Olivier's nickname was Larry. 'various' makes HPYASLARRY, and the A-plus-P pair goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was known as Larry, so being 'like Olivier' is jokingly being like Larry, i.e. very cheerful.

clue.text: Article in Times mostly full of Hindu texts

indicators.note: in puts the article between the two time letters

parts.note: T stands for time, so times plural gives two of them
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: full means rich, as in a rich diet

explanation.surface: A newspaper article packed with Hindu scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper: it gives two T's.
explanation.definitionFit: The tantras are a body of Hindu and Buddhist scriptures; the adjective describes things relating to them.

clue.text: He exchanged letters amusingly before assuming power

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the word for before takes the power letter inside it

parts.note: sooner means before, earlier

explanation.surface: Someone swapped amusing letters before taking power.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rev. William Spooner, Oxford don, was famed for swapping the initial sounds of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford don gave his name to slips that transpose word beginnings, such as 'tasted the whole worm'.

clue.text: Beat the top five in the Open?

indicators.note: top five in says keep only the first five letters of the word for the open air, dropping the rest

parts.note: the open air is the outdoors

explanation.surface: Beating the leading five players at golf's Open Championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Open' suggests the golf championship, but it is the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a rival is to surpass or do better than them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Whatever happens in a Big Apple trial?

parts.note: the Big Apple is a nickname for New York, NY
a court case is a trial

explanation.surface: Whatever the outcome of a New York courtroom trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Apple is New York, abbreviated NY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning regardless, whatever the circumstances turn out to be.

clue.text: Reps? They're over opening beers among the lads

indicators.note: opening says the turned word is split open to take the beers inside
over signals turning that word back to front

parts.note: they refers back to the definition, the reps of the clue's start
ales are beers
lads are boys, sons

explanation.surface: Sales reps finishing up over beers with the lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' points back to the definition; turned 'over' it makes SPER, which 'opening' splits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Reps is short for representatives, people who sell a firm's products.

clue.text: Current regulators in Rio quoted US, not Spain

indicators.note: quoted means repeated in speech, so we hear the city name

parts.note: Rio, the Brazilian city, spoken

indicators.note: not removes the Spain letter from the word

parts.note: the US is the States
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone in Rio de Janeiro quotes US figures, excluding Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control electrical current, e.g. in a dimmer.

clue.text: Rocks cover edge where docks 4

indicators.note: cover means surround, so the swaying word goes round the edge

parts.note: rocks means sways, moves to and fro
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: Rocks cover the edge of a dock where ships decline and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is DECLINE AND FALL: a slipway is the sloping ramp at a dock down which ships slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipways are the inclined ramps in shipyards and docks, slopes down which a hull runs into water.

clue.text: Recycle and reuse submarine

indicators.note: recycle says the letters of the next words are processed into something new

explanation.surface: An instruction to recycle and reuse an old submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' is an adjective here, not a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means existing beneath the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Left Janet dancing with Andrew, like Brucie?

indicators.note: dancing says the names are moving about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Janet and Andrew take to the floor, as on Bruce Forsyth's Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Brucie is Sir Bruce Forsyth, British TV host of Strictly Come Dancing, famous for his long jutting chin.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a long thin face with a prominent jaw, which was Bruce Forsyth's signature look.

clue.text: How many watched TV rebuke?

definitions.meaning: a viewing figure for a programme
a scolding or telling-off, from the verb to rate

explanation.surface: How many watched a TV telling-off?
explanation.definitionFit: Television audience figures are called ratings, and an old sense of rate means to scold, so the noun means a reprimand.

clue.text: Mark to retain hedges on road

indicators.note: hedges means encloses, so the proofreading mark surrounds the other letters

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep the hedges along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedges' looks like roadside hedgerows but is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, lined with buildings.

clue.text: Start to pull fast one, nearly drunk in common

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: nearly drops the final letter

parts.note: full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Pulling a fast one while nearly drunk in the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast one' tempts as a trick, but 'fast' is LENT and 'one' is I.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful means abundant, existing in great quantity, so something common in occurrence.

clue.text: Mixer unwrapped, put on ice

indicators.note: unwrapped says strip away the outside of the following words to reveal what sits within

explanation.surface: A mixer is opened and chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a mixer, a drink added to spirits such as gin.

clue.text: Hardly any are able to cut stone

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so the able word goes inside

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
can means are able

explanation.surface: Few people can cut stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, very little in amount.

clue.text: Team whose manager swaps European for a novice

indicators.note: swaps signals that one letter in the manager's name is exchanged for others

parts.note: Arsène Wenger, long-time manager of the London football club
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A football club whose manager trades a European player for a raw newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsène Wenger managed Arsenal, a London football club, from 1996 to 2018; L is the learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is an English football club, so this is an example of a team.

clue.text: Make concrete expand to cover each line

indicators.note: to cover means to surround, so the expanding word goes round the others

parts.note: to rise is to swell or expand, as dough does

explanation.surface: Building instructions: mix concrete to expand and cover each line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concrete' is an adjective, not the building material.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a plan is to make it real or actual, giving it tangible form.

clue.text: Notice a knock occasionally intruding during this?

definitions.text: Notice a knock occasionally intruding during this?

indicators.note: intruding says those letters push their way inside the noticing word

parts.note: to notice is to see

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of the word knock

explanation.surface: At a spiritualist sitting, people notice the odd knock interrupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' gives NC from kNoCk.
explanation.definitionFit: At a séance, participants listen for knocks believed to come from spirits.

clue.text: Parade ground command's not right in a sense

indicators.note: not removes the right letter from the command

parts.note: 'Eyes right!' is an order to turn heads on parade

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant's order isn't right, in some sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight, or vision, is one of the five senses.
